linkedin:
Remote hiring managers read applications on a screen, between meetings, often in a second language. The applications that get a reply are the ones that are easy to scan and clearly written for this role.

Lead with the exact job title and where you saw it. Then say in one sentence why your recent work fits. Save the background for later.

Show proof of async work: a project with written updates, a shared document you owned, or a time zone gap you handled well.

Match their words: if they say 'customer support', don't write 'client care'. Hiring software and tired humans look for the same words.

Keep your CV short: one clean page, most recent remote or freelance work first, with what you shipped.

Follow up once, politely, after a week. A single clear follow-up reads as professional; more reads as pressure.

Full guide: http://fixtures:8000/no-numbers-post.md
